narrative: The model estimated a 31% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. That does not mean default is certain; it means your estimated risk was above the bank’s acceptable cutoff, so the application was denied. Of the factors considered, your checking-account status was the strongest influence and was the main reason for denial. Your account was below zero DM, an overdrawn position seen for only about 12.6% of approved applicants, compared with 59.2% who had no overdraft; this pushed the decision toward bad credit. The second most important factor worked in your favour: your installment rate was 2% of disposable income, below the approved average of about 2.99%, which reduced perceived risk. The third most important factor also helped: your requested 12-month duration was shorter than the approved average of about 19.17 months, which also pushed toward good credit. Those two favourable factors were not enough to outweigh the checking-account concern. Next, ask the bank to verify that the overdrawn status is correct and discuss how to bring the account current or arrange an agreed overdraft. Ask for a manual review, and consider reapplying after regularising the account or adding a suitable guarantor, while keeping the loan term and repayments affordable.
